messages:
SupportBot: New incoming ticket AC-892 from customer 'Acme Apps' — they report broken JSON in json_mode=structured. Error seen by customer: "JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 5 column 3". They attached the raw response and a parser stack trace.

Mia (Support): thanks, grabbing the artifacts. can you paste the exact raw response body + the curl you used? also: model name and whether streaming was enabled.

Mia (Support): forwarding to @Ajay (API) and @Emily (ML) for triage.

Ajay (API): I looked at the request metadata — customer used model 'redwood-llm-13b' with streaming=true and json_mode=structured. curl snippet they used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-llm-13b","json_mode":"structured","stream":true,"input":"generate items array"}'
```

Ajay (API): they also included a small client that concatenates stream chunks and then JSON.parse()s the result.

Mia (Support): pasted the raw stream capture from customer (they joined chunks with no extra framing):

```
{"items":[{"id":"a1","val":10},{"id":"a2","val":15},
{"id":"a3","val":20,"extra":"foo"}{"id":"a4","val":25}],"meta":{"count":4}}
```

Emily (ML): immediate red flag: notice between the 3rd and 4th item there's no comma: `..."extra":"foo"}{"id":"a4"...` That's invalid JSON. Looks like a chunk boundary dropped a delimiter. with streaming, if the model emits a comma at the end of a chunk but the client concatenation logic reorders or trims, consumers can hit this.

Lucas (SRE): also saw intermittent 502s and then quick reconnects in request logs around the time the customer tested. If the stream reconnect drops a tiny token (comma) it's enough to corrupt the whole payload when concatenated.

Ajay (API): reproducer plan: call the same model with stream=true and intentionally split the returned tokens across two TCP writes to simulate chunk boundaries; verify that naive concat -> JSON.parse fails. quick test shows parser fails ~12% of the time when chunk cut occurs between tokens.

Mia (Support): customer is blocked because their parser is strict (they cannot accept partial objects). they asked whether we guarantee fully-formed JSON for json_mode=structured when streaming.

Emily (ML): short answer: we do not guarantee consumer-level framing on raw streaming output; structured mode aims for valid JSON overall but streaming can expose intermediate invalid prefixes. we should recommend either: 1) use non-streaming (stream=false) to get single validated JSON payload, or 2) use our framing wrapper (we expose chunk metadata headers) — if you need streaming, parse by Redwood framing rather than naive concat.

Ajay (API): action items: 1) doc update: clarify json_mode + stream semantics and recommend framing or stream=false for strict parsers. 2) add a server-side check that final non-streamed output is valid JSON before returning success (we already do this for non-streaming). 3) short-term: add a small compatibility note in API error responses when we detect client-side parse failures (support-facing).

Lucas (SRE): ops note: investigate the reconnects/502s — if stream interruptions are frequent we need to reduce chance of token loss. flagged infra team.

Mia (Support): I replied to customer with repro steps (curl non-streaming) and a workaround: set stream=false or wrap parsing to tolerate chunk-boundary fixes (e.g., incremental JSON parser). Customer says they need streaming for progress; suggested we expose per-chunk validity metadata or add an optional framed-stream mode.

Emily (ML): long term: consider producing framed JSON streaming (boundary markers) or emitting top-level newline-delimited JSON objects (NDJSON) when streaming structured arrays so incremental parsers can operate safely. picked up as product request.

Mia (Support): closing loop for now — customer accepted interim workaround (set stream=false for strict parsing). keeping this thread open until infra and docs actions are done. :thumbsup:
